title: Older Americans Feel Guilty Spending Savings
paragraphs: Many of us spend our whole lives trying to save money for the future. But we may spend so long trying to save that, when we finally do have money, it's hard to feel OK using it.

In fact, a new survey from US financial services company Prudential Financial found that 86% of Americans aged 50 and older don't feel comfortable spending money on things they enjoy, such as travel, hobbies and dining out.
And that's not just people who don't have savings — even among those with at least $500,000 in savings and investments, 61% still don't feel comfortable spending money on fun things for themselves.

Prudential says part of the problem is "FORO" — "fear of running out." Between things like inflation, healthcare costs, and just not knowing how long they'll live after they retire, people are worried about running out of money — and they just feel better when they have savings.
Among those with savings, more than a quarter say they feel proud when they see their total hasn't decreased. And 40% say they would rather leave money behind than risk running out.

Meanwhile, spending can bring feelings of guilt. Around 60% say they feel guilty spending on big trips and adventures, while 67% find it difficult to justify paying someone else to do jobs such as cleaning or gardening.
However, it's those who haven't retired yet that are the most worried. Those who have already retired are more likely to say they're not having as many money problems as they thought they'd have.

Prudential says having a clear plan may help people enjoy using the money they've saved. And the survey found that people with a retirement plan or a clear way of taking money from their savings are more likely to feel comfortable spending it.
